answer: Sybils survive only while coordination costs less than honesty, so the economy prices coordination directly. Credit is released only after peers from clusters that rarely co-sign together attest it; attestation inside a known ring decays to zero weight, so each identity must convince outsiders, who lose score if their endorsement traces there. The kernel never inspects intent, it prices trust, so a closed ring pays open-market rates. A hundred wallets cost a hundred reputations. The canyon between identities stops paying: a whisper among accomplices costs what a public statement costs.
